questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — gitjira (Jira-style tracker: Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL API, React board, npm workspaces). Verified finding: `createIssue()` reads the column's highest `position` with the global client before its transaction opens and appends `keyBetween(last, null)`, so two creates into one column can store the same key; once two neighbours tie, `keyBetween` throws for any drop between them. Separately, `moveIssue()` persists whatever `position` string the client sends, and the move schema only asks for a non-empty string. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: simultaneous creates into one column end with pairwise-distinct position keys, and no move can store a key that is malformed or that fails to sort strictly between the neighbours of its drop slot.

[w3] Guarded form: the last-key read runs on the transaction client AFTER the project counter increment, whose row lock already serializes creates in one project, so the second create reads the first one's committed key; merely moving the read inside the transaction without that ordering fixes nothing under read committed.

[w2] Scope includes the move path: the server checks the client key (alphabet, a length cap, strictly between the neighbours it reads inside the move transaction) and, on a tie or a bad key, regenerates one from those neighbours instead of storing the client's string; the check is exported once from the shared module.

[w2] Allowed files: apps/api/src/services/issue.service.js, packages/shared/src/fractional-index.js and issue-schemas.js, plus new or extended tests in apps/api/test/ and packages/shared/test/; the web board helpers stay as they are.

[w3] Boundary: fractional indexing stays the design, so a move still writes one issue row, with no renumbering, no rebalancing job and no migration; the in-place type change that left old rows with non-base-62 positions and the missing (column, position) index are reported, not fixed.

[w2] Test command: `npm test -w @gitjira/shared` for the pure property tests, then `npm test -w @gitjira/api` against the docker-compose PostgreSQL; the new race case opts out of rollback isolation at module load, as the issue-number race suite does.

[w2] Stop condition: a concurrent-create case asserting distinct keys and a move case with an out-of-order key are both red on the original and green on the fix, the existing move tests still pass, and if no database is reachable the agent stops and says so instead of reporting the API suite green.
keyPoints.quote: Two users dropping onto the _same_ gap can produce equal-ish keys

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What will an agent most likely get wrong here, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It moves the findFirst into the transaction ahead of the counter update and calls it done; with no lock taken first, two creates still read the same last key, and a sequential test cannot tell the difference. The 'after the increment' line and the race test prevent it.
[w3] It 'solves' ordering by switching to integers or renumbering the column on every write, which throws away the property the ADR chose fractional keys for.
keyPoints.quote: A move writes exactly ONE row — no renumbering, ever.

keyPoints.text: [w2] It wraps the throwing utility in a try/catch and falls back to storing the client's key, hiding the tie instead of regenerating past it.

[w2] It adds a unique index on (column, position) or a backfill migration in the same diff; a unique index turns a lost race into a failed create, and the no-migration boundary keeps that decision out of this change.

[w1] False green: it runs only the shared package's tests, which need no database, or writes the race case inside the default rollback wrapper, where both creates share one transaction and can never collide.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent hands back a diff and a green run. What do you check before accepting it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] In createIssue the position lookup now uses tx and sits after the counter update; no read of the last position through the global prisma client is left before the transaction.
[w3] The new race case sets the no-rollback flag, fires the creates at once into one column, asserts distinct keys, and the handback shows it failing on the original service.
[w2] moveIssue still updates a single issue row, the cross-project column move still answers 404, and the original move tests pass unchanged.
[w2] There is one key-validity check, in the shared package, used by both the schema and the service, and the existing property tests of keyBetween still pass beside its new cases.
[w1] The handback lists the follow-ups it saw but left alone: old rows' positions from the type change, collation-dependent ordering, and the deferred rebalancing.
keyPoints.quote: The production answer is periodic rebalancing; out of scope at our scale, noted for later.
